sections.title: Income tax: individuals (Rarotonga)
sections.basis: taxable income of an individual resident on Rarotonga for the income year (1 January to 31 December); the $14,600 exemption is prorated by days present for part-year residents
sections.note: The Revenue Management Division's quick reference guide gives these as the 2021-2023 rates; the 2025 individual return (Rarotonga) applies the same $14,600 exemption and bands (next $15,400 at 17%, next $50,000 at 27%, 30% above) and the PAYE schedule from 1 January 2021 is still the current one. No later change was found. Pa Enua (outer island) residents have a larger exemption (separate row).

rows.label: Income tax: exemption for Pa Enua (outer island) residents
rows.note: exemption on the 2025 individual return for Pa Enua (outer island) residents, prorated by days present. Under review: the 2025 Pa Enua return deducts a $60,000 exemption and then applies 27% and 30% with an $80,000 step, but the form's text does not show clearly whether the 27% band ends at $80,000 of income or after a further $80,000. Owner check against the Income Tax Act amendment for the Pa Enua.

rows.label: PAYE: employer withholding
rows.value: Employers deduct PAYE using the Rarotonga or Pa Enua PAYE schedules and file the RM205 VAT/PAYE return and pay by the 20th of the following month; RM101 tax deduction certificates go to employees and the RM106 PAYE reconciliation to RMD after the year end
rows.note: The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).
